newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends up as colder temps approach.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends up as colder temps approach.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil extended its gains Thursday as colder temperatures were seen hitting the U.S. northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
But, traders said the larger trend for oil prices was still bearish.

"The basic bear trend is still in place, but we have some good fundamentals surrounding heat right now, like colder temperatures and a drop in distillate supply," said John Bradberry, vice president at Continental Ozark Inc, a petroleum distributor in Arkansas. December heating oil settled up 0.44 cent at 66.89 cents a gallon.
Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney, forecasted temperatures would be 10 to 14 degrees below normal from Sunday to Tuesday in the northeastern United States.

Heating oil buoyed crude and gasoline, which traders said would have slipped if heating oil had not propped up the oil complex. December crude settled up five cents at $22.74 a barrel while December gasoline ended up 0.17 cent at 63.80 cents a gallon.
"There was plenty of downside in crude," said a trader, who added crude was only briefly able to sit above $23.00 before slipping near Wednesday's price levels.
Undermining gasoline and crude was the latest oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) that showed large supply builds, dealers said.

The API said Tuesday that crude stocks grew 9.3 million barrels for the week ended November 1 while gasoline stocks grew 4.7 million barrels. In contrast, distillate supplies, which heating oil is component, dropped 429,000 barrels.
Continental Ozark's Bradberry said distillate stocks are still about 30 percent below a year ago even though distillate production is at a high 3.6 million barrels a day.
Distillate stocks showed a significant build two weeks ago after refiners began focusing on distillate output following months of historically low stock levels.
The market turned bearish on news of building distillate stocks, and heating oil prices are 10 cents a gallon below their post-Gulf War highs reached in early October.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
